stack_spec.name: Built with Spec4 (BWS4)
stack_spec.description: A unified, self-hosted web app that showcases Spec4 through a gallery of example apps demonstrating agentic AI patterns: RAG, tool use, an embeddings explorer, single call, chained calls, a plan-first planning agent, a ReAct loop, orchestrated subagents, multi-agent collaboration (A2A-shaped) and a Router with measured agreement history and a no-router cost comparison.

languages.name: Python
languages.role: backend service: REST API, shared framework services (generation, embedding, search, storage, usage limiting, moderation, peer message bus), every example app's server-side logic, SSE streaming, and the Alembic SQL migrations for Neon Postgres; run as a single always-on Uvicorn process under systemd
languages.linter: Ruff (no extend-exclude entries: every package, router, service, test and main.py under backend/ is linted)
languages.type_checker: mypy (strict, no exclusions: the whole backend including main.py, older routers, services and tests is checked)

languages.name: TypeScript
languages.role: browser client: single-page app presenting the landing page and all example apps (built with Node 20+)
languages.formatter: none (no formatter installed; style kept by convention and review)

targets.name: web_client
targets.purpose: the browser UI presenting the landing page and every example app, with per-example-app code-splitting so the gallery can grow without bloating the initial load
targets.hosting: static files served directly by Caddy from the netcup VPS at the canonical public origin, same origin as the API
targets.build: Vite build producing a hashed static bundle with route-based lazy-loaded chunks per example app, built on the VPS by the deploy script (npm ci && npm run build) into dist/, which Caddy serves with SPA history fallback; VITE_* variables (VITE_API_BASE_URL, VITE_SENTRY_DSN) are build-time only and must be supplied in the shell that runs the frontend build, because the systemd EnvironmentFile does not reach npm run build
targets.distribution: served at the app's root domain, the gallery's single canonical public address

exposure.transport: HTTPS only, with automatic Let's Encrypt certificate issuance and renewal by Caddy and automatic HTTP to HTTPS redirection

targets.name: api
targets.purpose: serves the SPA's data needs: shared framework services plus every example app's endpoints (RAG, tool use, embeddings, single call, chained calls, planning agent, ReAct loop, orchestrated subagents, multi-agent collaboration, Router), moderation, Exa search integration, usage limiting and SSE streaming
targets.runtime: Python 3.12 under Uvicorn as a single always-on process (--workers 1, async concurrency only; never multiple workers or Gunicorn, because the loaded embedding model, fitted PCA projection, in-process peer message bus and ReAct duplicate-guard cache are per-process state) on a netcup VPS 500 G12 (2 vCores, 4 GB RAM, 128 GB NVMe); startup refuses to proceed if GROQ_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY is missing; the FastAPI lifespan warm-up then loads the embedding model, fits the 2D projection and derives the Router's route descriptions once at boot, each step best-effort (a failure is logged and the API still boots)
targets.hosting: self-hosted on the project's netcup VPS 500 G12, supervised by systemd (Restart=always, enabled at boot, EnvironmentFile on a root-owned 0600 file outside the repository), fronted by Caddy which reverse-proxies /api/* to Uvicorn on localhost
targets.build: deploy script run on the VPS (ssh -t rcrowe@<vps> '/srv/bws4/deploy/deploy.sh'): git pull, uv sync from pyproject.toml/uv.lock, frontend build, uv run alembic upgrade head, then systemctl restart of the service unit
targets.api_contract: REST; OpenAPI schema auto-generated by FastAPI; long-running run endpoints (planning, ReAct, orchestrated, collab, Router) stream JSON envelopes as server-sent events over POST; the ReAct trace is also retrievable via GET /api/react/run/{run_id}; the Router exposes POST run (staged SSE: decision card, routed answer or low-confidence card, cost strip, end-of-run event), POST rerun, GET presets (route descriptions, margin, cost order, and an availability flag that is false while route descriptions are not ready), GET history (agreement counts, typical-latency baseline with sample size) and a Retry action that re-attempts the route-description warm-up without an API restart; runs that never began (moderation flagged, fail-closed, shared cap too close, Router descriptions unavailable) return ordinary error responses instead of a stream and reserve no usage units

exposure.transport: HTTPS only, terminated by Caddy at the edge with automatic Let's Encrypt certificates; Uvicorn binds only to localhost and is never directly reachable from the network
exposure.cors: allow only the single non-wildcard configured browser origin (CORS_ORIGIN); the SPA is served from the same origin as the API, so the policy is exercised chiefly in local development

capabilities.capability_class: a capable general-purpose model for grounded, structured-output answers

a fast model with reliable JSON-schema-conforming output for single prompt/response work: the single-call demo, the Router's route classification (output retries zero), the ReAct suitability check and hop-source annotation, the disagreement note, and the collaboration reveal and sensitivity explanations
a capable model able to sustain a distinct role-played persona across a two-step sequential chain

a capable model with reliable structured output (and native tool-calling for the planning agent) able to decompose a goal into a validated small plan, and to emit per-cycle typed thought and action for the ReAct loop
a capable model with reliable structured output able to choose two specialists from a fixed roster and brief them, answer a briefed sub-question as a knowledge-only specialist, and merge two answers

a capable model with reliable structured output and persona adherence able to hold a private-constraint-bound negotiating position across bid, counter and best-and-final turns and to award against stated priorities

Groq (via LiteLLM and PydanticAI).credentials_env: GROQ_API_KEY (required in every environment: production, local development and the test suite; the API refuses to start without it; no placeholder value and no opt-out flag)
Groq (via LiteLLM and PydanticAI).fallback: OpenRouter free models take over through the shared ordered model chain (services/model_registry.py and agent_runtime.py, used by both the LiteLLM and PydanticAI lanes) when Groq is rate-limited, metered out for that model, retired, or unavailable; a Router classification call that fails or returns a schema-invalid object is not retried (output retries zero)

capabilities.capability_class: a capable free general-purpose model for grounded, structured-output answers
a fast free model with reliable typed or JSON-schema output for all single-call work, including the Router's classification call
a free model able to sustain a role-played persona across a two-step chain
a free model with reliable structured output and tool-calling for planner, executor and ReAct cycle calls
a free model with reliable structured output for delegation, specialist and merge calls
a free model with reliable structured output and persona adherence for any of the six negotiation turns

integrations.name: Exa Search API
integrations.purpose: ranked real web search results (title, snippet, source) through the single shared wrapper services/web_search.py, called directly in-process (no MCP) by the tool-use integration, the planning agent's research steps, the ReAct loop's act step, and the Router's search_generation route
integrations.auth: API key; EXA_API_KEY, read from the systemd EnvironmentFile on the VPS, never committed

integrations.name: OpenAI Moderation API (omni-moderation-latest)
integrations.purpose: pre-dispatch safety screening of free-form visitor input only (orchestrated subagents, ReAct loop, Router free text), free of charge so it does not consume model quota; runs before any allowance hold and fails closed; preset input skips it and the collaboration app never calls it
integrations.protocol: REST over HTTPS; POST /v1/moderations via httpx, parsed into a Pydantic ModerationVerdict
integrations.auth: API key; OPENAI_API_KEY, required in every environment (production, local development and the test suite) with no placeholder and no opt-out flag; read from the systemd EnvironmentFile, never committed

integrations.name: Sentry
integrations.purpose: optional error tracking and model-call performance spans (token usage, latency, error rate) on backend and frontend; no-ops when the DSN is unset
integrations.auth: DSN; SENTRY_DSN and SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT (backend), VITE_SENTRY_DSN (frontend, build-time only)

primary_store.purpose: durable relational store for everything the app writes, doubling as the vector index for the RAG example (whose retriever the Router reuses unchanged) and holding the Router's two shared append-only histories; external and managed, so the VPS migration does not change where data lives
primary_store.durability: source of truth; survives restarts, redeploys and the host migration because it is external to the VPS

collections.name: stored_records
collections.purpose: the shared storage abstraction's generic key-addressed retention records for apps that keep small pieces of information through the shared retention capability

collections.name: usage_limits
collections.purpose: the showcase-wide model/search allowance gate enforced server-side before every provider call by every example app, windowed per UTC hour and per UTC day
physical: usage window column keyed to the current UTC hour, plus the per-UTC-day cap window

collections.name: allowance_holds
collections.purpose: reserve/redeem/refund records against the shared usage gate so a run's full call budget is held before its first model call and a run that cannot finish is never started; the Router holds 2 units after moderation and before the router call and releases the second once the evaluator accepts; a comparison re-run holds only the expected route's dispatch cost; a Router run refused because route descriptions are unavailable takes no hold
physical: index on capability and usage window

collections.name: moderation_log
collections.purpose: safety-gate telemetry for free-form input: a salted hash of the question (never raw text), category, confidence, latency and whether the call failed closed
physical: salted question hash column; no raw question text column

collections.name: negotiation_runs
collections.purpose: the immutable per-run negotiation record written at run end: scenario, priority weighting, RFQ, both bid rounds, counters, award, reveal and sensitivity payloads, stage timings, model_calls_used and degradation flags

collections.name: peer_messages
collections.purpose: one row per A2A-shaped peer message, foreign-keyed to negotiation_runs, so the message log is a stored projection and the no-seller-to-seller claim is a single SQL predicate
physical: JSONB work-item column carrying the Task/Message/Artifact payload

collections.name: react_runs
collections.purpose: the per-run ReAct trace record written at run end and read back whole by GET /api/react/run/{run_id}: ordered cycles, terminal card, suitability verdict and hop-source annotations
physical: queryable header columns: question_origin, searches_used, cycle_budget, ending, duplicate_queries_blocked, empty_observations, suitability verdict fields, annotation_outcome

collections.name: router_agreement_records
collections.purpose: Append-only, shared-across-visitors record of one row per qualifying preset run, from which per-preset agreed/disagreed/declined counts, rates and the overall rate are computed in SQL; free-text runs, comparison re-runs and malformed-decision fallbacks write no row; a low-confidence tie-break landing on the expected route is recorded 'declined' and earns no credit; cells show counts only until 5 observations
physical: outcome column constrained to agreed / disagreed / declined
added by the same single Alembic migration as router_latency_observations

collections.name: router_latency_observations
collections.purpose: Append-only, shared-across-visitors record of one row per real search_generation-route run (comparison re-runs excluded), from which the rolling median behind the cost strip's 'typical' baseline is computed in SQL over the most recent N rows; sample size is the row count; below 5 observations the baseline is shown as counts only
physical: route column holding the route id (search_generation)
added by the same single Alembic migration as router_agreement_records

collections.name: service_log_entries
collections.purpose: the shared services' per-call log: which capability was invoked, by which example app, outcome and usage accounting, for every generation, embedding, search and moderation call

embedding_projection_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of preconfigured embeddings + fitted scikit-learn PCA model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 vectors), loaded and fitted once in the FastAPI lifespan at boot
embedding_projection_cache.purpose: fills the vector_index substrate for the embeddings example: holds the preconfigured examples' embeddings and fitted projection so custom text is transformed into the same stable 2D layout without recomputation and without persisting visitor text; built once at boot on the always-on VPS and kept warm
embedding_projection_cache.durability: ephemeral in-process derived state, rebuildable from bundled_assets' preconfigured_text_examples; never a source of truth; custom text embeddings exist only for the request

collections.name: preconfigured_example_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim per preconfigured example
fitted PCA model held in memory, reused via .transform() for custom text

react_query_guard_cache.choice: in-process NumPy array of the current run's issued-query embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via the shared service), held for one run
react_query_guard_cache.purpose: backs the semantic near-duplicate query guard so a rephrased repeat is blocked before it spends a search
react_query_guard_cache.durability: ephemeral; exists only for one run, discarded at its end, never persisted

collections.name: issued_query_embeddings
physical: in-process NumPy array, 384-dim per query issued so far in the run
cosine-similarity comparison against a tuned duplicate threshold (REACT_DUPLICATE_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD)

bundled_assets.choice: static content bundled at build time (typed Python literals and in-repo files)
bundled_assets.purpose: read-only content that changes only by code change and redeploy

collections.name: example_app_directory
collections.purpose: the single shared catalogue from which the landing-page listing and the site navigation are both driven, so they cannot disagree; includes 'ReAct Loop' and 'Router'

collections.name: preconfigured_text_examples
collections.purpose: the curated words, short phrases and sentences across categories that seed the embeddings plot

collections.name: preset_prompts
collections.purpose: curated example prompts (summarize, classify, extract) with their labelled intent, offered as one-click choices

collections.name: persona_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static, versioned system-prompt templates for the 'struggling writer' and 'harsh critic' personas

collections.name: planning_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static, versioned planner and synthesis prompt templates for the planning agent

collections.name: specialist_roster_config
collections.purpose: the fixed roster of four knowledge-only specialists (Technical, Financial, Historical, Practical), the closed set the coordinator must choose two from and against which the delegation decision is validated

collections.name: curated_presets
collections.purpose: curated preset questions chosen to produce different specialist pairings; pre-vetted so they bypass moderation

collections.name: orchestration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static, versioned coordinator delegation, specialist and merge prompt templates

collections.name: procurement_scenario_catalog
collections.purpose: pre-tuned procurement scenarios and selectable priority weightings, authored as version-controlled typed Python literals so mypy strict checks them

collections.name: sealed_private_constraints
collections.purpose: per scenario and per seller hidden negotiating position (cost floor, capacity ceiling, delivery capability, warranty liability limit) plus reveal seeds, authored as typed literals; sealing is enforced by the message bus's opacity policy at access time

collections.name: agent_identity_cards
collections.purpose: the three A2A-shaped identity cards (buyer plus two rival sellers): name, provider, skills, capabilities, and tool access of none

collections.name: collaboration_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static, versioned seller bid and best-and-final, buyer counter and award, and the two explanation prompt templates

collections.name: react_preset_catalog
collections.purpose: the five curated multi-hop preset questions with maintainer metadata (expected hops, which need observation); stores questions only, never answers

collections.name: react_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: static, versioned per-cycle, final-answer, suitability and hop-annotation prompt templates

collections.name: router_preset_catalog
collections.purpose: The six curated Router requests, each with an expected route and a one-line reason, including the two control/near-miss pairs; stores requests only, never answers; expected_route uses exactly the route ids deterministic_evaluator, single_call, retrieval and search_generation; typed Python literals

collections.name: router_unit_table
collections.purpose: The single source of truth for the deterministic evaluator's accepted language (operators, unit names and factors in length, speed and temperature, input length and nesting caps), read by the validator, the evaluator and the generated route description so they cannot drift

collections.name: router_route_descriptions
collections.purpose: The four one-line route descriptions generated at startup (never hand-written) from the unit table, the retriever's indexed document titles, the search tool's declared schema and the single-call capability's description, each with its cost_rank; shown byte for byte as the router received them; held in Router-module in-process state that is either ready or unavailable: a failed best-effort warm-up leaves it unavailable (the API still boots, the Router page shows 'temporarily unavailable' with Retry) and a successful Retry fills it without a restart

collections.name: router_prompt_templates
collections.purpose: The static, versioned route-classification prompt (request delimited as untrusted data) with its typed decision schema

collections.name: educational_overviews
collections.purpose: per-app short educational overview content, quota rationale and cross-references (Planning Agent and ReAct Loop; Router's contrast with Tool Use, Planning Agent and ReAct Loop and its uncalibrated-scores statement)

browser_local_storage.purpose: keeps small per-device visitor state and each app's advisory run counter and prior results so they survive navigating away and back
browser_local_storage.durability: per-device/browser only; not a source of truth; resettable by the visitor; hard quota protection is always the server-side usage gate

collections.name: theme_preference
collections.purpose: the visitor's chosen light/dark theme

collections.name: run_allowance
collections.purpose: advisory per-session run counter for the planning agent

collections.name: orchestrated_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the orchestrated-subagents three-run counter plus the visitor's prior run records, stamped with the UTC hour

collections.name: last_negotiation_run
collections.purpose: a cache of the visitor's most recent collaboration run, layered over the authoritative negotiation_runs and peer_messages persistence

collections.name: react_run_allowance
collections.purpose: the ReAct loop's two-run session counter plus the run_id and rendered trace of prior runs; the run_id lets the full trace be re-fetched from the server

collections.name: router_run_allowance
collections.purpose: The Router's advisory five-run counter plus the visitor's retained decision cards, routed answers and cost strips, stamped with the UTC hour; a comparison re-run costs one run and a refused run (including one refused because route descriptions are unavailable) costs none; the client decrements from the end-of-run event

chunking_pipeline.choice: hand-rolled paragraph/fixed-window text splitter, in application code
chunking_pipeline.purpose: splits reference_dataset documents into passages before embedding; kept simple and transparent for teaching clarity

embedding_pipeline.choice: sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), in-process, loaded once in the FastAPI lifespan at boot
embedding_pipeline.purpose: fills the embedding_pipeline substrate for RAG, the embeddings example and the ReAct near-duplicate guard: one shared model, never a second; stays resident for the process's lifetime so no visitor pays the load cost; the package is listed under libraries

retriever.choice: SQLAlchemy query using pgvector's cosine-distance operator against dataset_embeddings
retriever.purpose: finds the top-N passages for a question's embedding; the Router's retrieval route calls this existing retriever through its existing entry point, unmodified

pipeline_runner.choice: PydanticAI, using its OpenRouterProvider and native FallbackModel (slugs from the shared model registry) to run fixed sequences
pipeline_runner.purpose: fills the pipeline_runner substrate for the chained-calls writer-to-critic sequence (first response passed directly as the second call's input) and for the Router's classify, code-dispatch, optional-generation flow (one typed classification call with output retries zero, then code-owned dispatch); the usage gate checks every call exactly as on the LiteLLM path; no new dependency

agent_loop_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agent runs (FallbackModel over the shared chain) in two shapes: (a) planning agent: one structured-output planner call produces a validated Plan capped at 2-3 executor steps, executor steps run sequentially only after the visitor's Next; (b) ReAct loop: a hand-rolled bounded while-loop in backend/app/react/ where each cycle is one PydanticAI call returning a validated ReactStep, the slice executes the search between cycles and terminates on the model's answer decision or the ~8-search ceiling
agent_loop_runtime.purpose: fills the agent_loop_runtime substrate; the ReAct loop is hand-rolled so the cycle count is a code invariant the allowance hold can reserve against, every cycle boundary is an SSE emission point, and the duplicate guard runs between the chosen query and the search; the usage gate is checked before every model call

tool_execution_harness.choice: (a) planning agent: PydanticAI native tool-calling wrapping the shared Exa client (httpx) as a typed web-search tool; (b) ReAct loop and Router search_generation route: a direct in-process call to the shared Exa wrapper backend/app/services/web_search.py, with no tool registration and no MCP, the duplicate guard interposed for ReAct
tool_execution_harness.purpose: fills the tool_execution_harness substrate; the run-allowance check is a direct service-layer call, never a model-exposed tool, so the model cannot decide whether quota is spent; the Router reuses the shared wrapper rather than adding a harness

subagent_orchestration_runtime.choice: PydanticAI agents dispatched in-process and fanned out with asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True): a coordinator agent returns a validated DelegationDecision, then after the visitor's dispatch the two knowledge-only specialists run concurrently, then the coordinator merges
subagent_orchestration_runtime.purpose: fills the subagent_orchestration_runtime substrate; dispatching in code rather than a model-driven loop guarantees exactly three calls and genuine parallelism, and return_exceptions=True lets one specialist fail while the other's answer stays visible

agent_message_bus.choice: hand-rolled in-process message bus at backend/app/services/message_bus.py (append-only envelope store, deliver(message), context_for(agent_id) filtering strictly on recipient equality, chronological log projection) with a slice-local opacity policy layer in the collaboration app
agent_message_bus.purpose: fills the agent_message_bus substrate; peer opacity is enforced structurally in code, not by prompt; in-process state is one more reason for a single Uvicorn worker; injected via FastAPI Depends so tests can substitute it

protocol_runtime.choice: hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic models in backend/app/collab/protocol.py (AgentCard with AgentProvider/AgentSkill/AgentCapabilities, Task with TaskStatus/TaskState, Message with Role and Part/DataPart, Artifact), serialised camelCase, carried over the in-process bus with no HTTP, JSON-RPC or gRPC transport
protocol_runtime.purpose: fills the protocol_runtime substrate: implements A2A's data model and interaction pattern while deliberately omitting transport bindings; the overview states this plainly and what a real cross-owner deployment would add

tls_termination_and_static_serving.choice: Caddy 2 on the netcup VPS, serving the Vite dist/ bundle with SPA history fallback and reverse-proxying /api/* to Uvicorn on localhost, with automatic Let's Encrypt issuance and renewal and HTTP to HTTPS redirection, configured by a Caddyfile in deploy/
tls_termination_and_static_serving.purpose: one canonical public HTTPS origin that browsers trust, with certificate renewal built into the server; same-origin serving removes cross-origin traffic in production; Caddy does not buffer proxied responses, keeping the SSE example apps streaming progressively

process_supervision.choice: systemd service unit on the netcup VPS running a single Uvicorn process (--workers 1) under uv, Restart=always, enabled at boot, EnvironmentFile pointing at a root-owned 0600 secrets file outside the repository; logs to the journal alongside structlog JSON; Caddy runs under its own packaged unit
process_supervision.purpose: keeps the always-on instance running across crashes and reboots so the boot-time model load and PCA fit stay warm; holds the environment contract (DATABASE_URL, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, CORS_ORIGIN, optional SENTRY_DSN) outside the repository, with GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY enforced as required at startup; a single worker is mandatory because the loaded model, fitted projection, message bus and duplicate-guard cache are per-process state; the lifespan keeps embedding and Router route-description warm-ups best-effort so one failed optional step never blocks boot

release_delivery.choice: a shell deploy script in deploy/, run on the VPS: git pull, uv sync, npm ci && npm run build (VITE_* variables supplied in that shell), uv run alembic upgrade head, systemctl restart of the service unit; Node 20 and uv are installed on the host
release_delivery.purpose: one readable, version-controlled release procedure replacing the retired managed platform's pipeline; quality gates (ruff, mypy, pytest, oxlint, tsc, vitest) remain developer-run before push, as no CI exists; ruff and mypy now cover the whole backend with no exclusions

ai_conventions.prompt_versioning: every prompt-bearing slice stores its templates as versioned files in-repo under backend/app/<slice>/prompts/, tagged with a semantic version in the filename/header and loaded by a thin resolver function, with structured-output schemas defined alongside as versioned Pydantic models: rag/ (answer_v1.md), single_call/ (presets plus per-preset schema models), chained_calls/ (writer_v1.md, critic_v1.md), planning/ (planner_v1.md, synthesis_v1.md), orchestrated/ (delegation_v1.md, specialist_v1.md, merge_v1.md), collab/ (seller_bid_v1.md, seller_final_v1.md, buyer_counter_v1.md, buyer_award_v1.md, reveal_explanation_v1.md, sensitivity_v1.md), react/ (cycle_v1.md, final_answer_v1.md, suitability_v1.md, hop_annotation_v1.md) and router/ (route_v1.md with the typed RoutingDecision schema); schemas are kept narrow per call so a non-conforming response degrades only its own panel; no external prompt-management tool.

libraries.name: FastAPI
libraries.purpose: REST API framework, async-native, generates OpenAPI from Pydantic models

libraries.name: uvicorn
libraries.purpose: ASGI server running the app as a single always-on process under systemd, bound to localhost behind Caddy

libraries.name: SQLAlchemy
libraries.purpose: async ORM/toolkit for Neon Postgres including pgvector types, JSONB run records and the Router's SQL-computed agreement counts and rolling median

libraries.name: asyncpg
libraries.purpose: async PostgreSQL driver for SQLAlchemy's async engine

libraries.name: Alembic
libraries.purpose: versioned schema migrations (backend/app/db/migrations/versions/), applied by the deploy script; one migration adds the Router's two history tables

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.purpose: async HTTP client for the shared Exa wrapper (tool use, planning, ReAct, Router search route) and the OpenAI Moderation call

libraries.name: Pydantic
libraries.purpose: request/response validation and every slice's structured-output schemas, typed fixtures and the collaboration app's A2A-shaped protocol models

libraries.name: LiteLLM
libraries.purpose: unified interface to Groq and OpenRouter free models with retry and ordered fallback via model_registry.py; used by RAG, the single-call app and the Router's single_call and search_generation routes through the existing generation service

libraries.name: PydanticAI
libraries.purpose: agent framework (second model lane) returning validated Pydantic models via FallbackModel over the shared chain: chained calls, planning agent, orchestrated subagents, collaboration agents, ReAct per-cycle calls and annotation, and the Router's single typed classification call (output retries zero)

libraries.name: sse-starlette
libraries.purpose: server-sent events responses with keep-alive and client-disconnect detection so an abandoned run stops spending quota; streams the planning, orchestrated, collaboration, ReAct and Router runs

libraries.name: tenacity
libraries.purpose: bounded retry with backoff around outbound calls, including the moderation call before it fails closed

libraries.name: sentence-transformers
libraries.purpose: in-process embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) shared by RAG (including the Router's retrieval route), the embeddings example and the ReAct duplicate guard; no second embedding model is introduced

libraries.name: torch
libraries.purpose: inference backend beneath sentence-transformers, loaded at boot in the lifespan and kept resident

libraries.name: scikit-learn
libraries.purpose: PCA projection fitted once at boot on the preconfigured examples and reused via .transform() for custom text so the 2D layout stays stable

libraries.name: numpy
libraries.purpose: numeric arrays for embedding and PCA maths, the in-process projection cache and the ReAct cosine-similarity guard

libraries.name: pgvector
libraries.purpose: Python/SQLAlchemy client for the pgvector extension: vector columns and similarity queries, including the RAG retriever the Router reuses

libraries.name: pydantic-settings
libraries.purpose: typed environment-based configuration; GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are non-optional fields so startup fails with an error naming the missing credential (no placeholder, no opt-out flag, in production, local development and tests); on the VPS values arrive from the systemd EnvironmentFile with unchanged variable names

libraries.name: structlog
libraries.purpose: structured JSON logging for application events, service-log entries and per-run telemetry including the Router's online signals and logged warm-up failures; stdout captured by the systemd journal

libraries.name: sentry-sdk
libraries.purpose: backend error tracking and model-call spans (token usage, latency, error rates); optional, no-ops when SENTRY_DSN is unset

libraries.name: pytest

libraries.name: Ruff
libraries.purpose: Python linter and formatter, configured with no extend-exclude entries so the whole backend is gated

libraries.name: mypy
libraries.purpose: strict static type checking over the whole backend with no exclusions, and the reason scenario, preset and unit-table fixtures are typed Python literals

libraries.name: React
libraries.purpose: UI framework for the single-page app

libraries.name: react-dom
libraries.purpose: React DOM renderer

libraries.name: Vite
libraries.purpose: frontend build tool and dev server with code-splitting; the production build runs in place during deploy and emits dist/

libraries.name: @vitejs/plugin-react

project_structure.purpose: self-hosted deployment artifacts: the Caddyfile (single canonical origin, static dist/ with SPA history fallback, /api/* reverse proxy to Uvicorn on localhost, automatic Let's Encrypt TLS), the systemd unit template for the single-worker Uvicorn process (EnvironmentFile referencing a root-owned 0600 file outside the repo), deploy.sh (git pull, uv sync, npm ci && npm run build, alembic upgrade head, systemctl restart) and a README for first-time VPS provisioning; render.yaml is deleted from the repo root and no file may cite Render except to record its retirement

repository guidance for the coding agent; states the same environment contract as config and .env.example (GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY required in every environment, no placeholder, no opt-out; live smoke run opt-in)
example environment file listing every variable name (never values), with GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY marked required, consistent with CLAUDE.md and backend/app/core/config.py
thin FastAPI routers, one module per feature (landing, RAG, tool use, embeddings, single call, chained calls, planning, ReAct, orchestrated, collab, Router, shared services, health)
thin SSE router for the collaboration run (GET identity-cards, POST run) streaming one event per negotiation stage plus the explanation panels
thin router for the ReAct app: POST run streaming SSE envelopes (own DB session inside the generator, never Depends), GET run/{run_id}, GET presets (questions only), POST suitability

Thin router for the Router app: POST run (moderation for free text only, then the 2-unit hold, then staged SSE with its own DB session inside the generator), POST rerun, GET presets (including route-description availability), GET history, and a Retry action that re-attempts the route-description warm-up; refused runs, including those refused while descriptions are unavailable, return ordinary error responses with no hold; covered by ruff and mypy

shared framework services: LiteLLM generation wrapper, embedding, Exa web search (web_search.py), storage abstraction, model_registry.py and agent_runtime.py (all model calls go through these), and the usage-limit gate with reserve/redeem/refund holds; the Router calls these entry points unmodified apart from behaviour-neutral lint and type fixes
shared moderation service: moderate(text, calling_context) over httpx with tenacity retry, failing closed, logging only a salted hash, injected via Depends
shared in-process peer message bus with recipient-equality context filtering and a chronological log projection, injected via Depends

FastAPI entrypoint (now linted and type-checked): router registration, CORS pinned to the single configured origin, Sentry wiring, and the lifespan whose docstring describes the always-on VPS (embedding model and 2D projection load once at boot and stay warm); the embeddings warm-up and warm_route_descriptions() are both best-effort (failure logged via structlog, API still starts)
RAG logic: chunking, retriever, citation auditing, versioned prompts, curated dataset and indexing script
embeddings app logic: bundled TextItem set, in-process embedding and PCA fit/transform, custom-text route
single-call app logic: preset prompts, per-preset schema models and the route over the shared generation service
chained-calls logic: PydanticAI agents, the two-step writer-to-critic run (200 plus status 'critique_failed' contract preserved) and the route
versioned persona prompt templates
planning-agent logic: planner agent, plan validation and trimming to 2-3 steps, Exa tool registration, user-advanced executor run and SSE route
versioned planner and synthesis prompts with Plan/StepResult/Itinerary schemas

ReAct logic: preset catalog (questions only), moderation and suitability check, the hand-rolled bounded loop, per-cycle typed call, direct Exa calls, worst-case allowance reservation and refund, terminal-card selection, hop annotation, react_runs persistence and SSE emission
pure-function semantic near-duplicate query guard over (candidate, prior embeddings, threshold)
versioned ReAct prompts with their schemas
orchestrated-subagents logic: roster and presets, moderation gate, coordinator, asyncio.gather fan-out, merge, three-call reservation and SSE route
versioned delegation, specialist and merge prompts with schemas

collaboration logic: opacity policy over the bus, deterministic RFQ composer, buyer and seller agents, bid rounds, counter and award turns, explanation calls, eight-call reservation, NegotiationRecord persistence and SSE emission
hand-rolled A2A-shaped Pydantic models (AgentCard, Task, Message, Part, Artifact), camelCase
typed literal fixtures: scenarios, per-seller sealed constraints, priority presets and the three agent cards
versioned negotiation prompts with Bid/CounterOffer/Award and explanation schemas

Router logic (one-time check confirms it is covered by ruff and mypy): typed preset catalog, route-id constants (constants.py), generated route descriptions with a ready/unavailable state and a retryable warm_route_descriptions(), the classification agent (one PydanticAI call, output retries zero), margin check and fixed cost-order tie-break, malformed-decision handling, dispatch to existing single-call, RAG retriever and Exa-plus-generation entry points, comparison re-run, cost strip and baseline, history queries, 2-unit hold and release, staged SSE; named constants (margin, cost order, median window N) live here

Deterministic evaluator: closed-grammar tokenizer rejecting anything outside numbers, + - x /, parentheses, % and unit-table names, with length and nesting caps, and a recursive-descent evaluator; no ast, no eval, never executes model text; reads the unit table as the single source
Versioned route_v1.md with the typed RoutingDecision schema
SQLAlchemy models, async session factory and the Alembic migration tree (backend/app/db/migrations/versions/, including the migration for the Router's two history tables)
configuration (pydantic-settings, with GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY as required fields), structlog and Sentry setup (observability.py)

pytest suites mirroring the package layout, now gated by ruff and mypy like all backend code, including message-bus, collaboration-opacity and ReAct-loop invariant tests; all runs need real GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY; live-provider tests (-m live) opt-in; a type fix that would require changing a test is flagged, not made quietly

Router tests: evaluator grammar acceptance and rejection, caps, unit-table single-source and description generation, margin and cost-order tie-break, malformed-decision fallback, hold and release accounting, moderation-before-hold ordering, history inclusion rules, baseline thresholds, warm-up failure boot and Retry recovery, unavailable-state no-hold behaviour
one folder per screen: visitor (landing and example app tab strip) and maintainer
one folder per example app (rag, tool-use, embeddings, single-call, chained-calls, planning, react, orchestrated, collab, router), each lazy-loaded via its own route
embeddings route module: react-plotly.js plot, custom-text input, overview
single-call route module: prompt input and presets, Simple/Structured toggle, request/response views, overview
chained-calls route module: request input, upfront role description, labelled intermediate and final outputs, quota notice, overview
planning route module: city/interests input, plan display, Next button, progressive step results, itinerary, run allowance, limit notices, overview cross-referencing ReAct Loop

ReAct route module: overview, preset selector and free-form input, start control with no plan and no mid-run approval, cycle trace, live cycle counter, runs-remaining indicator, terminal cards, hop-source panel; its frontend tests are inspected and documented in the review note
orchestrated route module: presets and free-form input, delegation panel, Next dispatch, two parallel specialist columns, merged answer, runs-remaining counter, disabled state, overview
collaboration route module: scenario and priority selectors, agent cards, buyer track, two seller columns, reveal and sensitivity panels, message log, stated call cost, candid overview
hand-rolled Tailwind message-log table, one row per envelope with expandable JSON, making the absence of seller-to-seller rows visible

Router route module: overview, knowledge panel with route descriptions byte for byte beside the decision margin, six presets and free text, runs-remaining counter and exhausted state, a 'temporarily unavailable' state with a Retry button (shown instead of the input when the presets endpoint reports descriptions unavailable; a successful retry restores the page without reload of the API), decision card, Router-local wrappers importing existing Single Call, RAG and Tool Use presentational components unchanged, deterministic-result view, cost strip, comparison re-run view, agreement table with overall rate, and its own SSE consumption; the four route ids mirror backend/app/router/constants.py in frontend/src/api/router.ts and change together
shared UI: nav bar, theme toggle, layout shell and the shared markdown renderer wrapper
typed API client and TanStack Query hooks calling same-origin /api/*, plus SSE hooks for the planning, ReAct, orchestrated, collaboration and Router runs
route configuration with lazy imports per example app and the per-route SEO installer with canonicals at the single VPS origin (site and SEO metadata inspected and documented in the review note)
Vitest and React Testing Library suites for each app's user-visible behaviour

patterns: functional core / imperative shell: pure functions for chunking, retrieval scoring, PCA, schema validation, plan and delegation validation, the ReAct duplicate guard and terminal-card selection, RFQ composition, bus recipient filtering and opacity checks, and the Router's tokenizer, evaluator, margin check, tie-break, route-description generation and cost-strip arithmetic, with thin FastAPI handlers as the imperative shell

dependency injection for shared services (LiteLLM client, PydanticAI agents, DB session, Exa client, embedding service, moderation service, message bus) via FastAPI Depends so tests substitute them through app.dependency_overrides

concurrent agent work and iterative loops are owned by application code (asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True; the hand-rolled ReAct loop), not a model-driven tool loop, so call counts are code invariants the allowance reservation can rely on
peer visibility is enforced structurally, never by prompt: an agent's turn context is assembled only from envelopes the bus returns for that agent

routing is decided by the model and executed by code: the router makes exactly one typed call and stops; the low-confidence rule, torn-between pair (from the scores), cost-order tie-break and all dispatch live in code
model-produced text is never executed: the Router evaluator accepts only a closed grammar enforced by a tokenizer before parsing, with a hand-written recursive-descent evaluator and no ast or eval

Router run order is fixed: availability check (unavailable descriptions refuse the run with no hold), moderation (free text only), then the 2-unit hold before the first SSE event, then the router call, then staged events; a run refused before it begins consumes no run, takes no hold, has no ending state and writes no history row

Router history rules: only router-routed preset runs write an agreement row; free-text runs, comparison re-runs, malformed-decision fallbacks and lucky tie-breaks earn no credit; only real search_generation runs write a latency row; baseline time is always labelled 'typical'
routed answers reuse existing presentational components unchanged inside Router-local wrappers fed by props; the Router never reaches into another app's state or API hooks

zero lint and type exclusions: nothing may be added to Ruff or mypy exclusion lists; all backend code including main.py, older routers, services and tests is gated; cleanup fixes are behaviour-preserving, real bugs surfaced by findings are listed separately for the owner's decision, and no ongoing guard (pre-commit, CI) is added

optional startup steps are best-effort: the embeddings warm-up and warm_route_descriptions() each log failure via structlog and let the API start; required credentials are the only startup condition that is fatal
streaming routes open their own DB session inside the async generator via async_session_factory and never use Depends(get_db_session)

exactly one Uvicorn worker: in-memory state (embedding model, PCA projection, message bus, duplicate-guard cache, Router route-description state) is per-process by design; never add Gunicorn or multiple workers

all new model calls go through services/model_registry.py or services/agent_runtime.py so the shared allowance gate cannot be bypassed; free-tier model slug chains are refreshed periodically and never pinned in the spec

secrets are read only from the environment via pydantic-settings and never committed; no placeholder credential values exist anywhere, including tests; on the VPS they live in a root-owned 0600 file outside the repository
React: function components and hooks only, no class components; custom hooks for shared logic (useExampleApps, useTheme, useRunAllowance)
TypeScript has no formatter: oxlint, tsc and review enforce style; semicolons, trailing commas in multi-line structures and the 100-character line length are conventions
documentation: Google-style docstrings on every public Python function
JSDoc on every exported TypeScript function
every source file, Python and TypeScript, opens with the header comment 'Built with Spec4 AI - https://spec4.ai'
heavy explanatory comments stating why a decision was made; the deploy artifacts (Caddyfile, systemd unit, deploy script) follow the same convention
CLAUDE.md, backend configuration and .env.example must state the same environment contract

additional_decisions.name: groq_primary_supersedes_openrouter_only_constraint
additional_decisions.description: How the Groq provider relates to the vision's constraint that LiteLLM access only free OpenRouter models.
additional_decisions.value: Groq is recorded as primary and OpenRouter free models as fallback for every capability tier, matching the code (agent_runtime.py, GROQ_API_KEY). The vision constraint 'Must use LiteLLM to access only free LLMs provided by OpenRouter' is superseded by this and should be reworded in the next vision revision. Model slugs are not pinned in this spec; the developer pins current ones in the shared model registry.

additional_decisions.name: collaboration_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the multi-agent collaboration example app and how it is policed.
additional_decisions.value: 8 calls per run, disclosed as 6 negotiation calls (2 opening bids, 1 buyer counter, 2 best-and-final bids, 1 award) plus 2 post-award explanation calls (reveal, priority sensitivity); all 8 reserved via allowance_holds before the deterministic RFQ is composed; telemetry alerts when the negotiation-stage count differs from 6.

additional_decisions.name: react_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The declared per-run model-call budget for the ReAct loop and how it is reserved and released.
additional_decisions.value: Worst case 10 calls per run (up to 8 search-cycle calls, 1 final-answer call, 1 post-run hop-source annotation); the full worst case is reserved before the first cycle and the unspent remainder refunded when the loop answers early. The custom-question suitability check is 1 further call charged only on free-form input.

additional_decisions.name: router_run_call_budget
additional_decisions.description: The per-run model-call budget for the Router and how it is reserved, released and counted against the visitor's five runs.
additional_decisions.value: At most 2 model-call units per run including the classification call: 1 on deterministic_evaluator, 2 on other routes, plus one Exa search on search_generation. 2 units are reserved after moderation and before the router call; the second is released only once the evaluator has accepted the expression. Output retries are zero. Visitors get 5 runs per session (advisory localStorage counter); a comparison re-run counts as one, reserves only the expected route's dispatch cost, shows router overhead as an explicit zero and feeds no history; a refused run costs no run.

additional_decisions.name: router_malformed_decision_rule
additional_decisions.description: How a malformed router decision and evaluator rejections are handled; the AI spec supersedes the product spec's wording.
additional_decisions.value: A malformed or schema-invalid decision (no retry) dispatches to single_call with a plain card note, inside the routed-answer ending, with no agreement row; it is not 'declined', which is only the low-confidence outcome. If deterministic is chosen and the evaluator rejects the expression, dispatch goes to single_call with the unit held and the card states it as the router's own misroute; if a low-confidence tie-break lands on deterministic and the evaluator rejects, the other tied route is used and the card remains the low-confidence ending.

additional_decisions.name: router_route_ids
additional_decisions.description: Canonical spellings of the four Router route ids.
additional_decisions.value: deterministic_evaluator, single_call, retrieval, search_generation (cost order in that sequence), used identically in presets, the cost-order constant, the latency table, schemas and generated descriptions; defined in backend/app/router/constants.py and mirrored by hand in frontend/src/api/router.ts, changed together.

additional_decisions.name: router_named_constants
additional_decisions.description: Router tunables that are named constants in code so the page can print them.
additional_decisions.value: Decision margin, fixed cost order, rolling-median window N, the 5-observation minimum for baseline latency and each agreement cell, the evaluator's input length and nesting-depth caps, and the per-session run limit of 5.

additional_decisions.name: router_observability_signals
additional_decisions.description: Where the Router's online evaluation signals go.
additional_decisions.value: Schema-failure rate, argmax route distribution, margin distribution, evaluator fallback rate, router latency and route-description warm-up failures are emitted as structlog events and Sentry spans only; no table beyond the two history tables.

additional_decisions.name: router_warmup_unavailable_state
additional_decisions.description: How the Router behaves when its startup route-description warm-up fails, and how it recovers.
additional_decisions.value: warm_route_descriptions() is wrapped in the same best-effort handling as the embeddings warm-up: failure is logged and the API starts. The Router module holds a ready/unavailable state reported by GET presets; while unavailable the page shows 'temporarily unavailable' with a Retry button, no run starts and no usage units are reserved or spent. Retry re-attempts the warm-up without an API restart: success restores normal operation, failure keeps the same message. The other nine example apps are unaffected. No background retry timer is used.

additional_decisions.name: required_credentials_contract
additional_decisions.description: How GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are enforced and documented.
additional_decisions.value: Both are non-optional pydantic-settings fields, required in production, local development and the test suite; startup fails with an error naming the missing key. No placeholder values and no opt-out flag exist, so every pytest run needs real credentials; the live smoke run (-m live) remains opt-in. CLAUDE.md, backend/app/core/config.py and .env.example state the same contract. This is the one deliberate exception to the no-visible-change rule and affects only a misconfigured deployment.

additional_decisions.name: lint_type_gate_scope
additional_decisions.description: Scope and handling of the Ruff and mypy gate after the cleanup.
additional_decisions.value: All Ruff and mypy exclusions are removed so every backend package, router, service, test and main.py is gated; all findings are fixed and affected files reformatted; behaviour, routes, response shapes, usage caps and visitor messages (including Chained Calls' 200 with 'critique_failed' and the Router route-id contract) are unchanged; existing backend and frontend tests are the gate; a type fix that would require changing a test is flagged rather than made quietly; fixes for real bugs surfaced by findings are listed separately for the owner's decision. A one-time check confirms the Router package, api/router.py and backend/tests/router/ are covered; no pre-commit hook, CI job or other ongoing guard is added, and gates remain developer-run before push.

additional_decisions.name: unrecorded_edits_review_note
additional_decisions.description: How previously unrecorded edits are handled in this cleanup.
additional_decisions.value: The SEO and site metadata (page head, sitemap, per-route metadata), the shared generation service, README, Claude Code settings, pyproject.toml and the ReAct frontend test changes are each inspected and documented in a written review note; intentional changes stay, and anything that looks unintended is flagged for the owner's decision rather than reverted silently.

additional_decisions.name: deployment_downtime_posture
additional_decisions.description: How a release interacts with availability and warm start.
additional_decisions.value: A release is a plain systemctl restart: a brief outage while the embedding model load and PCA fit are re-paid at boot, borne by the deploy rather than a visitor. Zero-downtime deployment (a second warm instance and a Caddy upstream switch) was deliberately deferred.

additional_decisions.name: retired_hosting_configuration
additional_decisions.description: What is removed as part of retiring the previous host and what stays unchanged.
additional_decisions.value: render.yaml is deleted and the previous host serves nothing; the main.py lifespan docstring and all code, docs, configuration and deploy files are swept so Render is cited only where recording its retirement. The environment contract (DATABASE_URL, CORS_ORIGIN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, EXA_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, optional SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT and VITE_SENTRY_DSN) carries over with no variable added, removed or renamed; GROQ_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are required in every environment.
